I have farmed this land a long time, so I will keep the system steady and put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my income and food crop management, and it fits my well irrigation. My household labor is limited, so I will not spread myself too thin with too many complicated changes. I will keep a smaller area in cotton and stevia to maintain cash income, but I will not let them take too much land away from wheat and maize. On the wheat-maize land, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, put fertilizer where it gives me stable yield, and rely on a few timely irrigations rather than excessive watering. For cotton, I will keep inputs moderate because it needs more pest control and labor, and I do not want to overexpand it. For stevia, I will manage water and potassium more carefully because leaf yield and quality depend on steady growth. Overall, I will aim for stable production, manageable labor, and lower risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
